items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I asked Pat if he would do the record with

ctx.x: Right and then next to that shows, Live At The Mellon Jazz Festival in Philly in 1990. This one’s on “Jazz Door” so…

Well “Jazz Door” is a bootleg, that’s why. What they did was... It was done on a laserdisc and somebody just took the audio off of his stereo. It was all mixed and they put it out as a bootleg. A double-cd. We never got a penny for that. That was recorded, they didn’t even say it was from the Mellon Festival because you wouldn’t say where it was recorded from if you’re bootlegging. So it was recorded in Philadelphia. But at any rate, I had written these sequences, and I asked Pat if he would do the record with

me and Herbie. Pat at the time was using something call the Synclavier, which would sample at a high sample rate of 98hz. It had all these channels and Pat used to carry this whole thing around in the travel cases and take a tech to work on it. I wrote these sequences on my sequencer and they were transferred into the Synclavier. This is an interesting record because I didn’t use a bass player on it, the bass parts were then played in. I just wanted the three of us, Herbie and Pat (and myself) and be able to do…
